purpose: Define a small, trusted test set that proves the pipeline direction before expanding the system.
north_star: The project is successful only if real mixed-format source files become useful, trusted, searchable, linked Obsidian notes.
core_problem_this_solves: AI can write code where every line appears correct but the architecture is wrong.
A pipeline can process files successfully while producing low-value notes.
Extraction can appear to work while silently losing important content.
Tagging can look useful while failing to support retrieval or decision-making.
The system needs practical confidence before scaling.
golden_path_rule: Before adding more formats, OCR, media, or routing complexity, the system must pass the golden path test set.

golden_test_files.name: simple_markdown_note
golden_test_files.purpose: Prove the pipeline can process existing Obsidian-style text without damaging it.
expected_result: Does not over-transform simple useful notes

golden_test_files.name: plain_text_scrap
golden_test_files.purpose: Prove the gate can distinguish useful scraps from junk.
expected_result: Detects whether there is meaningful content
Routes obvious junk to review or low-value handling
Does not waste heavy LLM reasoning on empty noise

golden_test_files.name: text_pdf
golden_test_files.purpose: Prove normal PDF text extraction works.
expected_result: Does not mark text PDF as OCR-needed
Preserves title, dates, names, and key facts

golden_test_files.name: scanned_or_image_pdf
golden_test_files.purpose: Prove the system can detect OCR-needed documents safely.
expected_result: Does not treat failed extraction as scrap

golden_test_files.name: legacy_word_document
golden_test_files.purpose: Prove legacy Word is treated as different from modern Word.
expected_result: Returns ok, unsupported, corrupt, or metadata_only honestly
Never silently returns empty text as if the file has no value

golden_test_files.name: modern_excel_file
golden_test_files.purpose: Prove spreadsheet extraction creates useful summary, not unreadable table dump.
expected_result: Identifies whether this is invoice, budget, quote, job costing, or data reference

golden_test_files.name: legacy_excel_file
golden_test_files.purpose: Prove legacy Excel is treated separately from modern Excel.
expected_result: Preserves file provenance even if extraction is partial

golden_test_files.name: project_studios_business_file
golden_test_files.purpose: Prove business-area classification works for Project Studios.
expected_result: Topics may include SEO, PPC, web design, WordPress, lead generation, client work, or strategy

golden_test_files.name: super_clean_business_file
golden_test_files.purpose: Prove business-area classification works for Super Clean Services.
expected_result: Topics may include tenancy cleaning, carpet cleaning, window cleaning, quoting, customers, staff, jobs, invoices, or marketing
Preserves prices, dates, customer names, job details, and obligations
Does not reduce operational records to vague summaries

golden_test_files.name: how_to_or_technical_note
golden_test_files.purpose: Prove the system recognises procedural knowledge.
expected_result: Future question examples include how-to retrieval

golden_test_files.name: low_value_junk_file
golden_test_files.purpose: Prove the gate and review policy prevent garbage from becoming polished garbage.
expected_result: Low value_score unless a useful fact exists
Routed to review or low-value archive

stage_1_extract: Every file returns an ExtractionResult object.
Extraction failure must not equal empty content.
Legacy and modern formats must be separated.
stage_2_gate: Gate can send uncertain files to review.
Gate must not rely on LLM confidence.
stage_3_transform: LLM returns DecisionNote, not just tags.
DecisionNote includes summary, why_it_matters, key_points, facts, links, future questions, uncertainty, and discarded summary.
The result must be useful to Shaun in Obsidian.
The result must separate facts from interpretation.
stage_4_compose: Does not only create sidecar metadata.
stage_5_place_and_record: State is updated through one canonical StateManager.
Folders do not become the architecture.

hard_fail_if: Any file is silently treated as empty after failed extraction.
.doc is processed as if it were .docx.
.xls is processed as if it were .xlsx.
The LLM is called before the deterministic gate.
The output is only title, summary, tags, and confidence.
The system writes state using more than one schema.
Bash mutates state or performs data logic.
A low-value file becomes a polished fake-useful note.
Existing vault files can be overwritten without collision policy.
soft_fail_if: Business area is missing when obvious.
Raw excerpt is missing for high-value source material.
pass_fail_rules.pass_condition: At least 8 out of 10 reviewed golden path outputs, or an equivalent representative sample, must be clearly more useful than the raw source and must preserve trust/provenance.

confidence_types.extraction_confidence: Did we correctly read or classify the source file?
confidence_types.architecture_confidence: Did the file move through the proper stages without shortcuts?
confidence_types.knowledge_confidence: Did the output note recover useful value?
confidence_types.trust_confidence: Can Shaun see where the information came from and what is uncertain?

do_not: Do not write broad new extraction features yet.
Do not rewrite the whole project.
Do not optimise the legacy pipeline.
Do not create clever abstractions that are not required by the golden path.
Do not use passing code as proof of good architecture.
do: Create or review the golden path test plan first.
Map each test file to pipeline stages.
Identify what current code can already pass.
Identify what fails because of architecture.
Identify what fails because of missing libraries.
Identify what fails because of missing schemas.
Recommend the smallest next change that improves architectural confidence.

main_test_philosophy: The goal is not whether the script can run. The goal is whether the system can process a messy real-world sample without lying, losing value, or turning into spaghetti.
strong_summary: This test set is an architecture confidence harness. It proves that the pipeline can handle real mixed material, preserve trust, avoid silent failure, and produce useful Obsidian notes before scaling extraction, OCR, media handling, or folder routing. Passing means the system produces decision-ready knowledge. Failing means the architecture is still wrong, even if the code runs.
